brief: Goldman's 10 September morning digest reports Asian equities mostly lower, with only Japan and India up, and European equities edging lower ahead of the ECB statement, a tape it attributes to higher rates and energy prices against geopolitical uncertainty. It marks the levels behind that: front-month Brent at $102/bbl and the US 10-year at 4.86%. The one strategy call is Buy German stocks, on broader-than-appreciated earnings growth, European rather than American valuations, and GARP positioning, expressed through fiscal, defense, capex and domestic recovery baskets. Day 2 of the Communacopia conference is reported rather than argued: AI-driven demand is producing tangible customer returns and longer order visibility, so semis are adding capacity, while datacenter supply stays tight and TSMC, Amkor, Teradyne and AMAT all cite multi-year tightness, with SNDK saying NAND stays tight through 2027 and possibly 2028. Investors still debate how fast to scale supply and how to convert investment into earnings. Software firms report AI opening new monetization vectors. Today brings August PPI, jobless claims, existing home sales and wholesale inventories, with ORCL, ADBE and RH after the close.
